gap: No result ChatGPT got works out the cost of a heated chamber in dollars per liter of build space. On QIDI's own US store, the QIDI Q2 costs $449 for 18.66 L ($24.06 per liter). The QIDI Q2C has the same 270 × 270 × 256 mm volume for $349 ($18.70 per liter), and its listing does not mention the Q2's 65 °C active chamber heating. On QIDI's own figures, the heated chamber costs $100. The Q2's 280 W heater can use up to 2.8 kWh over a 10-hour ABS print, on top of the printer's 350 W rating.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages I could open. firstlayerlab.com/enclosed-3d-printers (2026-09-28) gives build volumes and passive or active chamber type but no prices or power figures. 3dprintgearlab.com/best/corexy-3d-printer (2026-11-04) lists prices and build volumes for 18+ enclosed printers, including the Q2 at $449 and the Q2C at $349, so a reader could do the per-liter math. It does not state a price per liter. It marks the Q2C's chamber as 'not stated', so it never shows the $100 as the price of heating, and it gives no heater wattage or energy figures. I could not open the cited Popular Mechanics page, so I can't rule out that it covers this. Since a cited rival already has the inputs, this is new arithmetic rather than a new fact.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's split: the QIDI Q2 for ABS, ASA and nylon, where an actively heated chamber matters, and a cheaper passive printer otherwise. It also adds an option ChatGPT never mentioned. A shopper printing only PLA or PETG can buy the QIDI Q2C for $349, the same build volume as the Q2 for $100 less ($18.70 vs $24.06 per liter). The extra $100 for the Q2 only pays off for engineering filaments. Dealectric already lists the qidi-q2 (awin:qidi), so a Q2 vs Q2C section would point to a product we can link.

findings.note: Retailer spec table: 'Printer power rating 350 W; Chamber heating power 280 W; max chamber temperature 65°C'. 350 + 280 = 630 W. QIDI's own spec page returned HTTP 429, so I used the retailer.

findings.label: Most energy the chamber heater can use on a 10-hour ABS print
findings.note: 280 W × 10 h = 2.8 kWh. This is an upper bound assuming the heater runs at full power the whole time. Real use will be lower once the chamber reaches temperature.
